description: The attestation challenge a receipt states, published as the bytes it hashes and the digest they give. Where a receipt's `enc` names a session arm, the value a platform quote must be bound to is sha256(nce || pk || req): the request nonce, the session public key the signed payload itself carries, and the digest of the exact request bytes, concatenated in that order and no other. Where `enc` states the plain arm, or the document is a version that names no arm, there is no key to fold and the value is sha256(nce || req), unchanged from what shipped. The arm the document states selects the rule, so no member names a ceremony and no new label exists for this: the registry and the member lists are untouched. Every triple is read out of a receipt this package publishes and signs, the pre-image is published as bytes because part order is a wire fact a sentence cannot pin, and each expected digest was computed twice before it was written: once by the shipped client derivation and once by concatenation here. `refusals` are the near readings: the other arm's rule over one of these documents, a key folded where the arm names none, and the same members in another order, each with the code the receipt-linked path owes it. What this suite does NOT pin is the platform's seal: no quote captured in this repository carries a composite, because a captured report data is fixed by the signature over it, so these rows pin the arithmetic and the owed second capture is stated in `layout.owedPlatformCapture` and in `docs/vectors.md` rather than left implied.

layout.format: one challenge rule, two arms, stated as pre-image bytes and the digest they hash to
layout.twin: the receipts this suite reads its triples out of are published and signed by generate.ts in data/manifest.json and data/receipts/
layout.reader: evidenceReportData in @ashaveri/sdk is the shipped derivation, and the pre-image published beside each digest is what an implementation with none of our code has to concatenate
layout.partOrder: the session arm is nce, then enc.pk, then req, and the plain arm is nce then req; the `parts` column states the order and the `preImageBase64Url` bytes are laid out in it, so a reader checks the order against the bytes rather than against its assumption
layout.challengeNonceIsNotTheSealNonce: nce is the request's challenge nonce, the value the platform is asked to quote; the AES-256-GCM nonce the session arm seals each leg with is a different value, never folded into this digest and never interchangeable with it
layout.encodings: byte strings unpadded base64url, digests lowercase hex, lengths in bytes
layout.owedPlatformCapture: A vector over a real platform quote whose report data carries a composite is owed to a capture. The Intel-signed quote under attest-core/test/fixtures has its REPORT_DATA fixed by Intel's own signature, so no test in this repository can ask it to carry sha256(nce || pk || req); these rows pin the arithmetic and the refusals name the codes, and the platform leg of the rule is witnessed when a confidential-VM deployment captures a quote over a composite.

vectors.name: plain-arm
vectors.note: The document whose `enc` states that both legs rode the wire in the clear. There is no key in it to fold, so the value a platform quote is bound to is `sha256(nce || req)` and it is byte for byte what this rule shipped before a key existed to fold: the plain arm is not a third reading, it is the old one, and a row that moved it would move every receipt served under it.

vectors.name: session-arm
vectors.note: The document whose `enc` names a session key. The same `nce` and `req` as the plain row above, and one more part between them, so the two rows differ by the arm alone and a reader that folded a key where the document names none, or named one where the document folds it, produces the other row value and is refused. The key is a fixture value this corpus derives from its own seed and no party holds it: the row pins the arithmetic over the bytes a receipt states, not a secret behind them.

refusals.name: session-arm-read-as-plain
refusals.note: The session document above, weighed as though its arm named no key: the reader hashes `nce || req` and asks the route with that. The deployment minted its evidence for the composite, so the bytes handed back are not the document the receipt digests into `att.d`, and the refusal is the receipt speaking rather than the platform.
refusals.wrongReading: sha256(nce || req) over a document whose `enc` names a key

refusals.name: plain-arm-folded-a-key
refusals.note: The plain document above, weighed as though its arm named a key, with the attestation digest `att.d` put where the key would go because the reader wanted three parts and the payload offers one beside the nonce. Nothing about this is a well-formed reading of the format: the arm states that no key was exchanged, so there is no part to insert, and a reader that inserted something anyway asks for an evidence document no receipt of this deployment commits to.
refusals.wrongReading: sha256(nce || att.d || req) over a document whose `enc` states `none`

refusals.name: parts-in-another-order
refusals.note: The three members of the session triple, right and concatenated request-last instead of request-middle: `sha256(nce || req || pk)`. This row exists because the members and the widths are identical to the accepted reading and only their order differs, which is exactly the disagreement a signature cannot see and a vector can: a quote whose field carries this value binds nothing a client on the stated order asked it to bind.
refusals.wrongReading: sha256(nce || req || pk), the stated members in another order
